nodes.name: Left Haar measure
nodes.statement: For a locally compact group $G$ let $\mu$ denote a left Haar measure of $G$.

nodes.name: Family B(G) of open compact subgroups (van Dantzig)
nodes.statement: Moreover, it is worth recalling immediately that a totally disconnected locally compact group $G$ has as a local base at $1$ the family $\mathcal B(G)$ of all open compact subgroups of $G$, as proved by van Dantzig in \cite{vD}.
differentia: of all open compact subgroups of $G$
nodes.statement_short: B(G), the open compact subgroups of a t.d.l.c. group, form a local base at 1 (van Dantzig).

nodes.name: phi-cotrajectory
nodes.statement: Let $G$ be a totally disconnected locally compact group and $\phi:G\to G$ a continuous endomorphism. For every $U\in\mathcal B(G)$ and every positive integer $n$, the \emph{$n$-th $\phi$-cotrajectory} of $U$ is $$C_n(\phi,U)=U\cap \phi^{-1}(U)\cap\ldots\cap\phi^{-n+1}(U),$$ and the \emph{$\phi$-cotrajectory} of $U$ is $$C(\phi,U)=\bigcap_{n=0}^\infty\phi^{-n}(U)=\bigcap_{n=1}^\infty C_n(\phi,U).$$
nodes.statement_short: $C_n(\phi,U)$ is the intersection of the first $n$ preimages of $U$; $C(\phi,U)$ is the intersection of all of them.

nodes.name: Basic properties of cotrajectories
nodes.statement: Note that $C_n(\phi,U)\in\mathcal B(G)$ for every positive integer $n$, while $C(\phi,U)$ is compact but not open in general, and it is the greatest $\phi$-invariant subgroup of $G$ contained in $U$. Moreover, for every positive integer $n$ the index $[U:C_n(\phi,U)]$ is finite as $U$ is compact and $C_n(\phi,U)$ is open.
nodes.statement_short: $C_n(\phi,U)$ is open compact with finite index in $U$; $C(\phi,U)$ is the largest $\phi$-invariant subgroup in $U$.

nodes.name: Topological entropy with respect to U
nodes.statement: The \emph{topological entropy of $\phi$ with respect to $U$} is given by the following limit, which is proved to exist in Lemma \ref{logalpha} below, $$H_{top}(\phi,U)=\lim_{n\to \infty}\frac{\log[U:C_n(\phi,U)]}{n}.$$
nodes.definiendum: topological entropy of $\phi$ with respect to $U$
nodes.statement_short: $H_{top}(\phi,U)$ is the exponential growth rate of the index $[U:C_n(\phi,U)]$.

nodes.name: Topological entropy
nodes.statement: The \emph{topological entropy} of $\phi$ is $$h_{top}(\phi)=\sup\{H_{top}(\phi,U):U\in\mathcal B(G)\}.$$

nodes.name: Limit-free formula for continuous endomorphisms
nodes.statement: Is it possible to extend the limit-free formula in \eqref{lff} to continuous endomorphisms of locally compact groups? Under which assumptions?

nodes.name: Tidying procedure formula for the scale function
nodes.statement: Indeed, it follows from the so-called tidying procedure given in \cite{Willis2} that $$s(\phi)=\min\{[\phi(C(\phi^{-1},U)):C(\phi^{-1},U)]:U\in\mathcal B(G)\};$$ so clearly $\log s(\phi)\leq h_{top}(\phi)$ in view of \eqref{lff}.
nodes.statement_short: Willis' scale is the minimal index $[\phi(C(\phi^{-1},U)):C(\phi^{-1},U)]$, hence $\log s(\phi)\le h_{top}(\phi)$.

nodes.name: Addition Theorem
nodes.statement: In \cite{St} the so-called Addition Theorem was proved for continuous endomorphisms $\phi:G\to G$ of compact groups; indeed, if $N$ is a closed normal $\phi$-invariant subgroup of $G$ and $\overline \phi:G/N\to G/N$ is the continuous endomorphism induced by $\phi$, then $$h_{top}(\phi)=h_{top}(\phi\restriction_N)+h_{top}(\overline\phi).$$
assumptions: $N$ is a closed normal $\phi$-invariant subgroup of $G$
$\overline \phi:G/N\to G/N$ is the continuous endomorphism induced by $\phi$

nodes.name: Addition Theorem for t.d.l.c. groups
nodes.statement: Let $G$ be a totally disconnected locally compact group, $\phi:G\to G$ a topological automorphism, $N$ a closed normal subgroup of $G$ such that $\phi(N)=N$, and $\overline\phi:G/N\to G/N$ the topological automorphism induced by $\phi$. Is it true that $h_{top}(\phi)=h_{top}(\phi\restriction_N)+h_{top}(\overline\phi)$?

nodes.name: Coset space and index
nodes.statement: For a group $G$ and a subgroup $H$ of $G$, we denote by $G/H$ the set of all (left) cosets of $H$ in $G$, and we denote by $[G:H]$ the index of $H$ in $G$, that is the size of $G/H$.

nodes.name: Generalized index [KH:H]
nodes.statement: If $K$ is another subgroup of $G$, then we denote by $KH/H$ the family of all (left) cosets of $H$ in $G$ with representing elements in $K$, that is $KH/H=\{kH:k\in K\}$, and we denote by $[KH:H]$ the size of this family, generalizing the usual notion of index.
nodes.statement_short: $KH/H$ is the set of cosets of $H$ with representatives in $K$; $[KH:H]$ is its size.

nodes.name: Index notation for H contained in K
nodes.statement: If $H\subseteq K$ then we write simply $K/H$ and $[K:H]$, as usual.

nodes.name: Index properties
nodes.statement: Let $G$ be a group and let $H,K,L$ be subgroups of $G$, with $H\subseteq K$. Then: \begin{itemize} \item[(a)] $[G:H]=[G:K][K:H]$; \item[(b)] $[LH:H]=[L:H\cap L]$; \item[(c)] $[K:H]\geq[K\cap L:H\cap L]$. \end{itemize} If $N$ is a normal subgroup of $G$, $q:G\to G/N$ is the canonical projection and $N\subseteq H$, then \begin{itemize} \item[(d)] $[K:H]=[q(K):q(H)]$. \end{itemize}
assumptions: $G$ be a group and let $H,K,L$ be subgroups of $G$, with $H\subseteq K$
$N$ is a normal subgroup of $G$, $q:G\to G/N$ is the canonical projection and $N\subseteq H$

nodes.statement_short: Multiplicativity of index, $[LH:H]=[L:H\cap L]$, monotonicity under intersection, and invariance under quotients.
nodes.label: gi

nodes.name: Stabilization of index ratios
nodes.statement: Let $G$ be a locally compact group, $\phi:G\to G$ a topological automorphism and $U\in\mathcal B(G)$. For every positive integer $n$ let $c_n:=[U:C_n(\phi,U)]$. Then: \begin{itemize} \item[(a)] $c_{n}$ divides $c_{n+1}$ for every $n>0$. \end{itemize} For every $n>0$ let $\alpha_{n}=\frac{c_{n+1}}{c_{n}}=[C_{n}(\phi,U):C_{n+1}(\phi,U)]$. Then: \begin{itemize} \item[(b)] $\alpha_{n+1}\leq\alpha_{n}$ for every $n>0$; \item[(c)] the sequence $\{\alpha_n\}_{n>0}$ stabilizes (i.e., there exist integers $n_0>0$ and $\alpha>0$ such that $\alpha_n=\alpha$ for every $n\geq n_0$); \item[(d)] $H_{top}(\phi,U)=\log\alpha$. \end{itemize}
assumptions: $G$ be a locally compact group, $\phi:G\to G$ a topological automorphism and $U\in\mathcal B(G)$
nodes.statement_short: The ratios $\alpha_n=[C_n:C_{n+1}]$ are non-increasing integers, hence eventually constant $=\alpha$, and $H_{top}(\phi,U)=\log\alpha$.
nodes.label: logalpha

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 2.2
nodes.statement: Let $n>0$. Since there is no possibility of confusion, in this proof we denote $C_n(\phi,U)$ simply by $C_n$. \smallskip (a) Since $U\supseteq C_n\supseteq C_{n+1}$ it follows from Fact \ref{gi}(a) that $[U:C_{n+1}]=[U:C_n][C_n:C_{n+1}]$, and so $\frac{c_{n+1}}{c_n}=[C_{n}:C_{n+1}]$; in particular $c_{n}$ divides $c_{n+1}$. \smallskip (b) Since $C_{n+1}=C_n\cap \phi^{-1}(U)$, and using Fact \ref{gi}(b), we have $$[C_n:C_{n+1}]=[C_n:C_n\cap \phi^{-n}(U)]=[C_n\cdot\phi^{-n}(U):\phi^{-n}(U)].$$ Now $C_n\subseteq \phi^{-1}(C_{n-1})$, so $$[C_n\cdot\phi^{-n}(U):\phi^{-n}(U)]\leq[\phi^{-1}(C_{n-1})\cdot\phi^{-n}(U):\phi^{-n}(U)].$$ The map $G/\phi^{-n}(U)\to G/\phi^{-n+1}(U)$ induced by $\phi$ is injective, therefore the family of cosets $(\phi^{-1}(C_{n-1})\cdot\phi^{-n}(U))/\phi^{-n}(U)$ has the same size of its image $(C_{n-1}\cdot\phi^{-n+1}(U))/\phi^{-n+1}(U)$, and so, applying also Fact \ref{gi}(b) and the fact that $C_n=C_{n-1}\cap \phi^{-n+1}(U)$, we have \begin{equation*}\begin{split} [\phi^{-1}(C_{n-1})\cdot\phi^{-n}(U):\phi^{-n}(U)]&=[C_{n-1}\cdot\phi^{-n+1}(U):\phi^{-n+1}(U)]=\\&=[C_{n-1}:C_{n-1}\cap \phi^{-n+1}(U)]=[C_{n-1}:{C_n}]. \end{split}\end{equation*} \smallskip (c) follows immediately from (b). \smallskip (d) By item (c) for $n_0>0$ we have $c_{n_0+n}=\alpha^n c_{n_0}$ for every $n\geq0$, and by the definition of topological entropy $$H_{top}(\phi,U)=\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{\log c_n}{n}=\lim_{n\to \infty}\frac{\log(\alpha^n c_{n_0})}{n}=\log\alpha,$$ and this concludes the proof.
nodes.statement_short: Index multiplicativity gives divisibility; injectivity of the induced coset map gives monotone ratios, which stabilize.

nodes.name: Notation C_n
nodes.statement: Let $n>0$. Since there is no possibility of confusion, in this proof we denote $C_n(\phi,U)$ simply by $C_n$.
nodes.statement_short: Abbreviate $C_n(\phi,U)$ as $C_n$.

nodes.name: (a) divisibility
nodes.statement: (a) Since $U\supseteq C_n\supseteq C_{n+1}$ it follows from Fact \ref{gi}(a) that $[U:C_{n+1}]=[U:C_n][C_n:C_{n+1}]$, and so $\frac{c_{n+1}}{c_n}=[C_{n}:C_{n+1}]$; in particular $c_{n}$ divides $c_{n+1}$.
nodes.statement_short: Apply Fact 2.1(a) to get $c_{n+1}/c_n=[C_n:C_{n+1}]$.

nodes.name: (b) monotone ratios
nodes.statement: (b) Since $C_{n+1}=C_n\cap \phi^{-1}(U)$, and using Fact \ref{gi}(b), we have $$[C_n:C_{n+1}]=[C_n:C_n\cap \phi^{-n}(U)]=[C_n\cdot\phi^{-n}(U):\phi^{-n}(U)].$$ Now $C_n\subseteq \phi^{-1}(C_{n-1})$, so $$[C_n\cdot\phi^{-n}(U):\phi^{-n}(U)]\leq[\phi^{-1}(C_{n-1})\cdot\phi^{-n}(U):\phi^{-n}(U)].$$ The map $G/\phi^{-n}(U)\to G/\phi^{-n+1}(U)$ induced by $\phi$ is injective, therefore the family of cosets $(\phi^{-1}(C_{n-1})\cdot\phi^{-n}(U))/\phi^{-n}(U)$ has the same size of its image $(C_{n-1}\cdot\phi^{-n+1}(U))/\phi^{-n+1}(U)$, and so, applying also Fact \ref{gi}(b) and the fact that $C_n=C_{n-1}\cap \phi^{-n+1}(U)$, we have \begin{equation*}\begin{split} [\phi^{-1}(C_{n-1})\cdot\phi^{-n}(U):\phi^{-n}(U)]&=[C_{n-1}\cdot\phi^{-n+1}(U):\phi^{-n+1}(U)]=\\&=[C_{n-1}:C_{n-1}\cap \phi^{-n+1}(U)]=[C_{n-1}:{C_n}]. \end{split}\end{equation*}
nodes.statement_short: Use Fact 2.1(b) and injectivity of the map induced by $\phi$ on cosets to get $\alpha_n\le\alpha_{n-1}$.

nodes.name: (c) stabilization
nodes.statement: (c) follows immediately from (b).
nodes.statement_short: A non-increasing sequence of positive integers stabilizes.

nodes.name: (d) entropy value
nodes.statement: (d) By item (c) for $n_0>0$ we have $c_{n_0+n}=\alpha^n c_{n_0}$ for every $n\geq0$, and by the definition of topological entropy $$H_{top}(\phi,U)=\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{\log c_n}{n}=\lim_{n\to \infty}\frac{\log(\alpha^n c_{n_0})}{n}=\log\alpha,$$ and this concludes the proof.
nodes.statement_short: Compute the limit with $c_{n_0+n}=\alpha^n c_{n_0}$.

nodes.name: Topological entropy takes values in log N_+
nodes.statement: Lemma \ref{logalpha} yields that the limit defining the topological entropy exists, and gives a precise description for the value of the topological entropy $H_{top}(\phi,U)$ of a topological automorphism $\phi:G\to G$ of a totally disconnected locally compact group $G$ with respect to $U\in\mathcal B(G)$; in particular, this value is in $\log\mathbb N_+$, so the value $h_{top}(\phi)\in\log\mathbb N_+\cup\{\infty\}$.
nodes.statement_short: The limit defining $H_{top}$ exists and lies in $\log\mathbb N_+$, so $h_{top}\in\log\mathbb N_+\cup\{\infty\}$.

nodes.name: Intersection lemma for descending chains
nodes.statement: \emph{\cite{DG-limitfree}} Let $G$ be a topological group and let $T$ be a closed subset of $G$. Then for every descending chain $B_1 \supseteq B_2 \supseteq \ldots \supseteq B_n \supseteq \ldots$ of closed subsets of $G$ the intersection $B = \bigcap_{n=1}^\infty B_n $ is non-empty and $\bigcap_{n=1}^\infty (B_{n} T)= B T$, whenever $B_1$ is countably compact.
assumptions: $G$ be a topological group and let $T$ be a closed subset of $G$
descending chain $B_1 \supseteq B_2 \supseteq \ldots \supseteq B_n \supseteq \ldots$ of closed subsets of $G$
$B_1$ is countably compact
nodes.label: intersect

nodes.name: Limit-free formula for topological entropy
nodes.statement: Let $G$ be a totally disconnected locally compact group, $\phi:G\to G$ a topological automorphism and $U\in\mathcal B(G)$. Then $$H_{top}(\phi,U)=\log[\phi(C(\phi^{-1},U)):C(\phi^{-1},U)].$$
assumptions: $G$ be a totally disconnected locally compact group, $\phi:G\to G$ a topological automorphism and $U\in\mathcal B(G)$
nodes.statement_short: $H_{top}(\phi,U)$ equals the log of the index of $C(\phi^{-1},U)$ in its image under $\phi$.
nodes.label: lf+

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 2.4 (limit-free formula)
nodes.statement: By Lemma \ref{logalpha} there exist integers $n_0>0$ and $\alpha> 0$ such that $\alpha_n=\alpha$ for every $n\geq n_0$, where $\alpha_{n}=[C_{n}(\phi,U):C_{n+1}(\phi,U)]$ for every $n>0$, and $H_{top}(\phi,U)=\log\alpha$. So it suffices to prove that \begin{equation} [\phi(C(\phi^{-1},U)):C(\phi^{-1},U)]=\alpha. \end{equation} Since $C(\phi^{-1},U)=U\cap \phi(C(\phi^{-1},U))$, and by Fact \ref{gi}(b), we have \begin{equation}\begin{split} [\phi(C(\phi^{-1},U)):C(\phi^{-1},U)]&=[\phi(C(\phi^{-1},U)):U\cap \phi(C(\phi^{-1},U))]\\&=[\phi(C(\phi,U))\cdot U:U]. \end{split}\end{equation} The family of cosets $(\phi(U)\cdot U)/U$ is finite, as $U$ is open and $\phi(U)\cdot U$ is compact, since both $U$ and $\phi(U)$ are compact. Consequently, the sequence $\{(\phi(C_n(\phi^{-1},U))\cdot U)/U\}_{n>0}$ is a descending chain of finite subsets of $(\phi(U)\cdot U)/U$ (note that $\phi(C_1(\phi^{-1},U))=\phi(U)$), hence it stabilizes, that is there exists $n_1>0$ such that \begin{equation} \phi(C_n(\phi^{-1},U))\cdot U=\phi(C_{n_1}(\phi^{-1},U))\cdot U\ \text{for every}\ n\geq n_1; \end{equation} in other words, \begin{equation} \bigcap_{n=1}^\infty (\phi(C_{n}(\phi^{-1},U))\cdot U)=\phi(C_{n_1}(\phi^{-1},U))\cdot U. \end{equation} Now Lemma \ref{intersect} gives \begin{equation} \bigcap_{n=1}^\infty (\phi(C_{n}(\phi^{-1},U))\cdot U)=\left(\bigcap_{n=1}^\infty \phi(C_n(\phi^{-1},U))\right)\cdot U=\phi(C(\phi^{-1},U))\cdot U, \end{equation} since $\bigcap_{n=1}^\infty \phi(C_n(\phi^{-1},U))=\phi(C(\phi^{-1},U))$. Therefore, \eqref{n1n}, \eqref{iot} and \eqref{lemmagives} yield \begin{equation} \phi(C(\phi^{-1},U))\cdot U=\phi(C_{n_1}(\phi^{-1},U)) \cdot U=\phi(C_{n}(\phi^{-1},U)) \cdot U\ \text{for every}\ n\geq n_1. \end{equation} Let $n\geq\max\{n_0,n_1\}$. Then \eqref{eqa} and \eqref{eqb}, together with Fact \ref{gi}(b), give \begin{equation}\begin{split} [\phi(C(\phi^{-1},U)):C(\phi^{-1},U)]&=[\phi(C(\phi^{-1},U))\cdot U:U]\\&=[\phi(C_n(\phi^{-1},U))\cdot U:U]\\&=[\phi(C_n(\phi^{-1},U)):\phi(C_n(\phi^{-1},U))\cap U]\\&=[\phi(C_n(\phi^{-1},U)):C_{n+1}(\phi^{-1},U)]. \end{split}\end{equation} Applying $\phi^{-n}$, we have the equalities $$\phi^{-n}(C_{n+1}(\phi^{-1},U))=C_{n+1}(\phi,U)\ \text{and}\ \phi^{-n}(\phi(C_n(\phi^{-1},U)))=C_n(\phi,U),$$ so, since $\phi^{-n}$ is an isomorphism, we have \begin{equation} [\phi(C_n(\phi^{-1},U)):C_{n+1}(\phi^{-1},U)]=[C_n(\phi,U):C_{n+1}(\phi,U)]=\alpha. \end{equation} By \eqref{split} and \eqref{lasteq} we can conclude that \eqref{aim} holds, so the thesis is proved.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to showing the index equals the stable ratio $\alpha$. A stabilizing descending chain of coset sets plus Lemma 2.3 identifies $\phi(C(\phi^{-1},U))U$ with $\phi(C_n(\phi^{-1},U))U$, and applying $\phi^{-n}$ gives $\alpha$.

nodes.name: Target index equality (2.1)
nodes.statement: [\phi(C(\phi^{-1},U)):C(\phi^{-1},U)]=\alpha.
nodes.label: aim

nodes.name: Index rewriting (2.2)
nodes.statement: \begin{split} [\phi(C(\phi^{-1},U)):C(\phi^{-1},U)]&=[\phi(C(\phi^{-1},U)):U\cap \phi(C(\phi^{-1},U))]\\&=[\phi(C(\phi,U))\cdot U:U]. \end{split}
nodes.label: eqa

nodes.name: Stabilization at n_1 (2.3)
nodes.statement: \phi(C_n(\phi^{-1},U))\cdot U=\phi(C_{n_1}(\phi^{-1},U))\cdot U\ \text{for every}\ n\geq n_1;
nodes.label: n1n

nodes.name: Intersection of chain (2.4)
nodes.statement: \bigcap_{n=1}^\infty (\phi(C_{n}(\phi^{-1},U))\cdot U)=\phi(C_{n_1}(\phi^{-1},U))\cdot U.
nodes.label: iot

nodes.name: Lemma 2.3 applied (2.5)
nodes.statement: \bigcap_{n=1}^\infty (\phi(C_{n}(\phi^{-1},U))\cdot U)=\left(\bigcap_{n=1}^\infty \phi(C_n(\phi^{-1},U))\right)\cdot U=\phi(C(\phi^{-1},U))\cdot U,
nodes.label: lemmagives

nodes.name: Stabilized product (2.6)
nodes.statement: \phi(C(\phi^{-1},U))\cdot U=\phi(C_{n_1}(\phi^{-1},U)) \cdot U=\phi(C_{n}(\phi^{-1},U)) \cdot U\ \text{for every}\ n\geq n_1.
nodes.label: eqb

nodes.name: Index chain (2.7)
nodes.statement: \begin{split} [\phi(C(\phi^{-1},U)):C(\phi^{-1},U)]&=[\phi(C(\phi^{-1},U))\cdot U:U]\\&=[\phi(C_n(\phi^{-1},U))\cdot U:U]\\&=[\phi(C_n(\phi^{-1},U)):\phi(C_n(\phi^{-1},U))\cap U]\\&=[\phi(C_n(\phi^{-1},U)):C_{n+1}(\phi^{-1},U)]. \end{split}
nodes.label: split

nodes.name: Apply Lemma 2.2
nodes.statement: By Lemma \ref{logalpha} there exist integers $n_0>0$ and $\alpha> 0$ such that $\alpha_n=\alpha$ for every $n\geq n_0$, where $\alpha_{n}=[C_{n}(\phi,U):C_{n+1}(\phi,U)]$ for every $n>0$, and $H_{top}(\phi,U)=\log\alpha$.
nodes.statement_short: Lemma 2.2 gives stable ratio $\alpha$ with $H_{top}=\log\alpha$.

nodes.name: Reduction
nodes.statement: So it suffices to prove that \begin{equation} [\phi(C(\phi^{-1},U)):C(\phi^{-1},U)]=\alpha. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to proving the index equals $\alpha$.

nodes.name: Rewrite index
nodes.statement: Since $C(\phi^{-1},U)=U\cap \phi(C(\phi^{-1},U))$, and by Fact \ref{gi}(b), we have \begin{equation} \begin{split} [\phi(C(\phi^{-1},U)):C(\phi^{-1},U)]&=[\phi(C(\phi^{-1},U)):U\cap \phi(C(\phi^{-1},U))]\\&=[\phi(C(\phi,U))\cdot U:U]. \end{split}\end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Rewrite the index as $[\phi(C)U:U]$ via Fact 2.1(b).

nodes.name: Chain stabilizes
nodes.statement: The family of cosets $(\phi(U)\cdot U)/U$ is finite, as $U$ is open and $\phi(U)\cdot U$ is compact, since both $U$ and $\phi(U)$ are compact. Consequently, the sequence $\{(\phi(C_n(\phi^{-1},U))\cdot U)/U\}_{n>0}$ is a descending chain of finite subsets of $(\phi(U)\cdot U)/U$ (note that $\phi(C_1(\phi^{-1},U))=\phi(U)$), hence it stabilizes, that is there exists $n_1>0$ such that \begin{equation} \phi(C_n(\phi^{-1},U))\cdot U=\phi(C_{n_1}(\phi^{-1},U))\cdot U\ \text{for every}\ n\geq n_1; \end{equation} in other words, \begin{equation} \bigcap_{n=1}^\infty (\phi(C_{n}(\phi^{-1},U))\cdot U)=\phi(C_{n_1}(\phi^{-1},U))\cdot U. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: A descending chain of finite coset sets stabilizes at some $n_1$.

nodes.name: Apply Lemma 2.3
nodes.statement: Now Lemma \ref{intersect} gives \begin{equation} \bigcap_{n=1}^\infty (\phi(C_{n}(\phi^{-1},U))\cdot U)=\left(\bigcap_{n=1}^\infty \phi(C_n(\phi^{-1},U))\right)\cdot U=\phi(C(\phi^{-1},U))\cdot U, \end{equation} since $\bigcap_{n=1}^\infty \phi(C_n(\phi^{-1},U))=\phi(C(\phi^{-1},U))$.
nodes.statement_short: Lemma 2.3 commutes intersection with multiplication by $U$.

nodes.name: Combine
nodes.statement: Therefore, \eqref{n1n}, \eqref{iot} and \eqref{lemmagives} yield \begin{equation} \phi(C(\phi^{-1},U))\cdot U=\phi(C_{n_1}(\phi^{-1},U)) \cdot U=\phi(C_{n}(\phi^{-1},U)) \cdot U\ \text{for every}\ n\geq n_1. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Combine to identify $\phi(C(\phi^{-1},U))U$ with $\phi(C_n(\phi^{-1},U))U$.

nodes.name: Index for large n
nodes.statement: Let $n\geq\max\{n_0,n_1\}$. Then \eqref{eqa} and \eqref{eqb}, together with Fact \ref{gi}(b), give \begin{equation} \begin{split} [\phi(C(\phi^{-1},U)):C(\phi^{-1},U)]&=[\phi(C(\phi^{-1},U))\cdot U:U]\\&=[\phi(C_n(\phi^{-1},U))\cdot U:U]\\&=[\phi(C_n(\phi^{-1},U)):\phi(C_n(\phi^{-1},U))\cap U]\\&=[\phi(C_n(\phi^{-1},U)):C_{n+1}(\phi^{-1},U)]. \end{split}\end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: For large $n$ the index equals $[\phi(C_n(\phi^{-1},U)):C_{n+1}(\phi^{-1},U)]$.

nodes.name: Apply phi^{-n}
nodes.statement: Applying $\phi^{-n}$, we have the equalities $$\phi^{-n}(C_{n+1}(\phi^{-1},U))=C_{n+1}(\phi,U)\ \text{and}\ \phi^{-n}(\phi(C_n(\phi^{-1},U)))=C_n(\phi,U),$$ so, since $\phi^{-n}$ is an isomorphism, we have \begin{equation} [\phi(C_n(\phi^{-1},U)):C_{n+1}(\phi^{-1},U)]=[C_n(\phi,U):C_{n+1}(\phi,U)]=\alpha. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Transport by $\phi^{-n}$ to get $[C_n(\phi,U):C_{n+1}(\phi,U)]=\alpha$.

nodes.name: Conclude
nodes.statement: By \eqref{split} and \eqref{lasteq} we can conclude that \eqref{aim} holds, so the thesis is proved.
nodes.statement_short: Conclude (2.1).

nodes.name: Modulus
nodes.statement: For a locally compact group $G$ and a left Haar measure $\mu$ on $G$, the \emph{modulus} is a group homomorphism $\Delta:\mathrm{Aut(G)}\to\mathbb R_+$ such that $\mu(\alpha E)=\Delta(\alpha)\mu(E)$ for every topological automorphism $\alpha\in \mathrm{Aut}(G)$ and every measurable subset $E$ of $G$ (see \cite{HR}).
nodes.section: 3 The topological entropy of the inverse automorphism
differentia: $\mu(\alpha E)=\Delta(\alpha)\mu(E)$ for every topological automorphism $\alpha\in \mathrm{Aut}(G)$ and every measurable subset $E$ of $G$

nodes.name: Modulus is trivial on compact groups
nodes.statement: If $G$ is compact, then $\Delta(\phi)=1$ for every topological automorphism $\phi:G\to G$.
nodes.section: 3 The topological entropy of the inverse automorphism
assumptions: $G$ is compact

nodes.name: Modulus as an index ratio
nodes.statement: Let $G$ be a totally disconnected locally compact group, $\phi:G\to G$ a topological automorphism and $U\in\mathcal B(G)$. Then \begin{itemize} \item[(a)] $\Delta(\phi)=\frac{\mu(\phi(U))}{\mu(U)}=\frac{[\phi(U):U\cap\phi(U)]}{[U:U\cap\phi(U)]}$. \item[(b)] If $V\in\mathcal B(G)$ and $V\subseteq U\cap \phi(U)$, then $[\phi(U):V]=[U:V]\cdot\Delta(\phi)$. \end{itemize}
nodes.section: 3 The topological entropy of the inverse automorphism
assumptions: $G$ be a totally disconnected locally compact group, $\phi:G\to G$ a topological automorphism and $U\in\mathcal B(G)$
$V\in\mathcal B(G)$ and $V\subseteq U\cap \phi(U)$
$V\in\mathcal B(G)$ and $V\subseteq U\cap \phi(U)$

nodes.statement_short: The modulus of $\phi$ is the ratio of indices $[\phi(U):U\cap\phi(U)]/[U:U\cap\phi(U)]$.
nodes.label: Delta

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 3.1
nodes.statement: (a) Follows from the fact that $\mu(\phi(U))=[\phi(U):U\cap \phi(U)]\cdot\mu(U\cap\phi(U))$ and $\mu(U)=[U:U\cap\phi(U)]\cdot \mu(U\cap\phi(U))$, since $U$ and $\phi(U)$ are compact and $U\cap\phi(U)$ is open, and so $[\phi(U):U\cap\phi(U)]$ and $[U:U\cap\phi(U)]$ are finite. \smallskip (b) The situation is described by the following diagram: $$\xymatrix{ U \ar@{-}[dr]& & \phi(U)\ar@{-}[dl] \\ & U\cap\phi(U)\ar@{-}[d] \\ & V & }$$ By Fact \ref{gi}(a) we have $$[U:V]=[U:U\cap\phi(U)][U\cap\phi(U):V]$$ and $$[\phi(U):V]=[\phi(U):U\cap\phi(U)][U\cap\phi(U):V].$$ Therefore, $$[\phi(U):V]=[U:V]\frac{[\phi(U):U\cap\phi(U)]}{[U:U\cap\phi(U)]}.$$ To conclude apply item (a).
nodes.section: 3 The topological entropy of the inverse automorphism
nodes.statement_short: Compare Haar measures of $U$, $\phi(U)$ through the common open subgroup $U\cap\phi(U)$, then use index multiplicativity.

nodes.name: (a) measure ratio
nodes.statement: (a) Follows from the fact that $\mu(\phi(U))=[\phi(U):U\cap \phi(U)]\cdot\mu(U\cap\phi(U))$ and $\mu(U)=[U:U\cap\phi(U)]\cdot \mu(U\cap\phi(U))$, since $U$ and $\phi(U)$ are compact and $U\cap\phi(U)$ is open, and so $[\phi(U):U\cap\phi(U)]$ and $[U:U\cap\phi(U)]$ are finite.
nodes.section: 3 The topological entropy of the inverse automorphism
nodes.statement_short: Express both measures via $\mu(U\cap\phi(U))$.

nodes.name: (b) index identity
nodes.statement: (b) The situation is described by the following diagram: $$\xymatrix{ U \ar@{-}[dr]& & \phi(U)\ar@{-}[dl] \\ & U\cap\phi(U)\ar@{-}[d] \\ & V & }$$ By Fact \ref{gi}(a) we have $$[U:V]=[U:U\cap\phi(U)][U\cap\phi(U):V]$$ and $$[\phi(U):V]=[\phi(U):U\cap\phi(U)][U\cap\phi(U):V].$$ Therefore, $$[\phi(U):V]=[U:V]\frac{[\phi(U):U\cap\phi(U)]}{[U:U\cap\phi(U)]}.$$ To conclude apply item (a).
nodes.section: 3 The topological entropy of the inverse automorphism
nodes.statement_short: Index multiplicativity plus item (a).

nodes.name: Entropy of the inverse automorphism
nodes.statement: Let $G$ be a totally disconnected locally compact group, $\phi:G\to G$ a topological automorphism and $U\in\mathcal B(G)$. Then $$H_{top}(\phi^{-1},U)= H_{top}(\phi,U)-\log\Delta(\phi).$$ Hence, $$h_{top}(\phi^{-1})=h_{top}(\phi)-\log\Delta(\phi).$$
nodes.section: 3 The topological entropy of the inverse automorphism
assumptions: $G$ be a totally disconnected locally compact group, $\phi:G\to G$ a topological automorphism and $U\in\mathcal B(G)$

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 3.2
nodes.statement: For every positive integer $n$ let $c_n=[U:C_n(\phi,U)]$ and $c_n^*=[U:C_n(\phi^{-1},U)]$. According to items (a)--(c) of Lemma \ref{logalpha} applied to $\phi$ and $\phi^{-1}$ respectively, $H_{top}(\phi,U)=\log\alpha$ and $H_{top}(\phi^{-1},U)=\log \alpha^*$, where $\alpha$ is the value at which stabilizes the sequence $\alpha_n=\frac{c_{n+1}}{c_{n}}$ and $\alpha^*$ is the value at which stabilizes the sequence $\alpha^*_n=\frac{c_{n+1}^*}{c_{n}^*}$. For every $n>0$, since $\phi^n(C_n(\phi,U))=C_n(\phi^{-1},U)$, using that $\phi^n$ is an automorphism, and by Lemma \ref{Delta}(b), we have that \begin{equation*}\begin{split} c_n &=[U:C_n(\phi,U)]=[\phi^n(U):\phi^n(C_n(\phi,U))]=\\&=[\phi^n(U):C_n(\phi^{-1},U))=[U:C_n(\phi^{-1},U)]\cdot\Delta(\phi^n)=c_n^*\cdot \Delta(\phi^n). \end{split}\end{equation*} Therefore, since $\Delta$ is a homomorphism, $$\alpha=\frac{c_{n+1}}{c_n}=\frac{c_{n+1}^*}{c_n^*}\cdot\frac{\Delta(\phi^{n+1})}{\Delta(\phi^n)}=\alpha^*\Delta(\phi),$$ hence we have the equality $\log\alpha=\log\alpha^*+\log\Delta(\phi)$, which gives the first assertion of the proposition. The second equality in the thesis follows from the first one taking the supremum for $U$ ranging in $\mathcal B(G)$.
nodes.section: 3 The topological entropy of the inverse automorphism
nodes.statement_short: Relate the indices for $\phi$ and $\phi^{-1}$ by $c_n=c_n^*\Delta(\phi^n)$ via Lemma 3.1(b), then compare stable ratios.

nodes.name: Stable ratios for phi and its inverse
nodes.statement: For every positive integer $n$ let $c_n=[U:C_n(\phi,U)]$ and $c_n^*=[U:C_n(\phi^{-1},U)]$. According to items (a)--(c) of Lemma \ref{logalpha} applied to $\phi$ and $\phi^{-1}$ respectively, $H_{top}(\phi,U)=\log\alpha$ and $H_{top}(\phi^{-1},U)=\log \alpha^*$, where $\alpha$ is the value at which stabilizes the sequence $\alpha_n=\frac{c_{n+1}}{c_{n}}$ and $\alpha^*$ is the value at which stabilizes the sequence $\alpha^*_n=\frac{c_{n+1}^*}{c_{n}^*}$.
nodes.section: 3 The topological entropy of the inverse automorphism
nodes.statement_short: Lemma 2.2 gives stable ratios $\alpha,\alpha^*$ for $\phi,\phi^{-1}$.

nodes.name: Relate c_n and c_n^*
nodes.statement: For every $n>0$, since $\phi^n(C_n(\phi,U))=C_n(\phi^{-1},U)$, using that $\phi^n$ is an automorphism, and by Lemma \ref{Delta}(b), we have that \begin{equation*}\begin{split} c_n &=[U:C_n(\phi,U)]=[\phi^n(U):\phi^n(C_n(\phi,U))]=\\&=[\phi^n(U):C_n(\phi^{-1},U))=[U:C_n(\phi^{-1},U)]\cdot\Delta(\phi^n)=c_n^*\cdot \Delta(\phi^n). \end{split}\end{equation*}
nodes.section: 3 The topological entropy of the inverse automorphism
nodes.statement_short: Lemma 3.1(b) gives $c_n=c_n^*\Delta(\phi^n)$.

nodes.name: Local formula
nodes.statement: Therefore, since $\Delta$ is a homomorphism, $$\alpha=\frac{c_{n+1}}{c_n}=\frac{c_{n+1}^*}{c_n^*}\cdot\frac{\Delta(\phi^{n+1})}{\Delta(\phi^n)}=\alpha^*\Delta(\phi),$$ hence we have the equality $\log\alpha=\log\alpha^*+\log\Delta(\phi)$, which gives the first assertion of the proposition.
nodes.section: 3 The topological entropy of the inverse automorphism
nodes.statement_short: Derive $\alpha=\alpha^*\Delta(\phi)$.

nodes.name: Global formula
nodes.statement: The second equality in the thesis follows from the first one taking the supremum for $U$ ranging in $\mathcal B(G)$.
nodes.section: 3 The topological entropy of the inverse automorphism
nodes.statement_short: Take the supremum over $U$.

nodes.name: Limit-free formula via the cotrajectory of phi
nodes.statement: Let $G$ be a totally disconnected locally compact group, $\phi:G\to G$ a topological automorphism and $U\in\mathcal B(G)$. Then $$H_{top}(\phi,U)=\log[\phi^{-1}(C(\phi,U)):C(\phi,U)]+\log\Delta(\phi).$$
nodes.section: 3 The topological entropy of the inverse automorphism
assumptions: $G$ be a totally disconnected locally compact group, $\phi:G\to G$ a topological automorphism and $U\in\mathcal B(G)$
nodes.label: lf-

nodes.name: Proof of Corollary 3.3
nodes.statement: Theorem \ref{lf+} applied to $\phi^{-1}$ gives $$H_{top}(\phi^{-1},U)=\log[\phi(C(\phi^{-1},U)):C(\phi^{-1},U)].$$ Moreover, Proposition \ref{^-1} yields $H_{top}(\phi,U)= H_{top}(\phi^{-1},U)+\log\Delta(\phi)$, hence the thesis follows.
nodes.section: 3 The topological entropy of the inverse automorphism
nodes.statement_short: Apply Theorem 2.4 to $\phi^{-1}$ and combine with Proposition 3.2.

nodes.name: Antimonotonicity of H_top
nodes.statement: Let $G$ be a totally disconnected locally compact groupa and $\phi:G\to G$ a continuous endomorphism. For any $U,V\in\mathcal B(K)$, if $U\subseteq V$, then $H_{top}(\phi,V)\leq H_{top}(\phi,U)$.
assumptions: $G$ be a totally disconnected locally compact groupa and $\phi:G\to G$ a continuous endomorphism
$U,V\in\mathcal B(K)$
$U\subseteq V$
nodes.label: antim

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 4.1
nodes.statement: Since $U\subseteq V$, we have that $C_n(\phi,U)\subseteq C_n(\phi,V)$ for every $n>0$. Then, also by Fact \ref{gi}(a) we have for every $n>0$ $$[V:C_n(\phi,V)]\leq[V:C_n(\phi,U)]=[V:U][U:C_n(\phi,U)].$$ Applying the definition of topological entropy, that is, taking the logarithm, dividing by $n$ and letting $n\to\infty$, we find that $H_{top}(\phi,V)\leq H_{top}(\phi,U)$.
nodes.statement_short: Bound $[V:C_n(\phi,V)]$ by $[V:U][U:C_n(\phi,U)]$, take logs, divide by $n$ and pass to the limit.

nodes.name: Inclusion of cotrajectories
nodes.statement: Since $U\subseteq V$, we have that $C_n(\phi,U)\subseteq C_n(\phi,V)$ for every $n>0$.
nodes.statement_short: $C_n(\phi,U)\subseteq C_n(\phi,V)$.

nodes.name: Index bound
nodes.statement: Then, also by Fact \ref{gi}(a) we have for every $n>0$ $$[V:C_n(\phi,V)]\leq[V:C_n(\phi,U)]=[V:U][U:C_n(\phi,U)].$$
nodes.statement_short: Bound the index via Fact 2.1(a).

nodes.name: Pass to the limit
nodes.statement: Applying the definition of topological entropy, that is, taking the logarithm, dividing by $n$ and letting $n\to\infty$, we find that $H_{top}(\phi,V)\leq H_{top}(\phi,U)$.
nodes.statement_short: Take logs, divide by $n$, let $n\to\infty$.

nodes.name: Proof of Corollary 4.2
nodes.statement: By the definition of topological entropy we immediately derive from Lemma \ref{antim} that, in order to compute the ``global'' topological entropy, it suffices to take the supremum when $U$ ranges in a local base at $1$ of $K$:
nodes.statement_short: Immediate from antimonotonicity (Lemma 4.1) and the definition of $h_{top}$.

nodes.name: Local base suffices for entropy
nodes.statement: Let $G$ be a totally disconnected locally compact group, $\phi:G\to G$ a continuous endomorphism and $\mathcal B\subseteq \mathcal B(G)$ a local base at $1$. Then $h_{top}(\phi)=\sup\{H_{top}(\phi,U):U\in\mathcal B\}$.
assumptions: $G$ be a totally disconnected locally compact group, $\phi:G\to G$ a continuous endomorphism and $\mathcal B\subseteq \mathcal B(G)$ a local base at $1$
nodes.label: basesuff

nodes.name: Invariance under conjugation
nodes.statement: Let $G$ be a totally disconnected locally compact group and $\phi:G\to G$ a topological automorphism. Let $H$ be another totally disconnected locally compact group and $\xi:G\to H$ a topological isomorphism. Then $\xi(C(\phi,U))=C(\xi\phi\xi^{-1},\xi(U))$ for every $U\in\mathcal B(G)$, and so $h_{top}(\phi)=h_{top}(\xi\phi\xi^{-1})$.
assumptions: $G$ be a totally disconnected locally compact group and $\phi:G\to G$ a topological automorphism
$H$ be another totally disconnected locally compact group and $\xi:G\to H$ a topological isomorphism
nodes.label: conj

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 4.3
nodes.statement: Let $\psi=\xi\phi\xi^{-1}$. It is clear that, for $U\in\mathcal B(G)$, \begin{equation} \xi(C(\phi,U))=C(\psi,\xi(U)). \end{equation} Since $\xi:G\to H$ is a topological isomorphism, it induces a bijection $\mathcal B(G)\to \mathcal B(H)$, so by Theorem \ref{lf+} it suffices to check that \begin{equation} [\phi(C(\phi^{-1},U)):C(\phi^{-1},U)]=[\psi(C(\psi^{-1},\xi(U))):C(\psi^{-1},\xi(U))]. \end{equation} From \eqref{uff} applied to $\phi^{-1}$ and $\psi^{-1}$ we have $C(\psi^{-1},\xi(U))=\xi(C(\phi^{-1},U))$, so, using also the fact that $\xi$ is an isomorphism, \begin{equation*}\begin{split} [\psi(C(\psi^{-1},\xi(U))):C(\psi^{-1},\xi(U))]=[\psi(\xi(C(\phi^{-1},U))):\xi(C(\phi^{-1},U))]=\\ =[\xi(\phi(C(\phi^{-1},U))):\xi(C(\phi^{-1},U))]=[\phi(C(\phi^{-1},U)):C(\phi^{-1},U)]; \end{split}\end{equation*} then \eqref{suff} is verified and this concludes the proof.
nodes.statement_short: By the limit-free formula it suffices to compare indices, which are preserved by the isomorphism $\xi$.

nodes.name: Conjugated cotrajectory (4.1)
nodes.statement: \xi(C(\phi,U))=C(\psi,\xi(U)).
nodes.label: uff

nodes.name: Conjugated cotrajectory
nodes.statement: Let $\psi=\xi\phi\xi^{-1}$. It is clear that, for $U\in\mathcal B(G)$, \begin{equation} \xi(C(\phi,U))=C(\psi,\xi(U)). \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Set $\psi=\xi\phi\xi^{-1}$ and note $\xi(C(\phi,U))=C(\psi,\xi(U))$.

nodes.name: Reduce via Theorem 2.4
nodes.statement: Since $\xi:G\to H$ is a topological isomorphism, it induces a bijection $\mathcal B(G)\to \mathcal B(H)$, so by Theorem \ref{lf+} it suffices to check that \begin{equation} [\phi(C(\phi^{-1},U)):C(\phi^{-1},U)]=[\psi(C(\psi^{-1},\xi(U))):C(\psi^{-1},\xi(U))]. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: By Theorem 2.4 reduce to an equality of indices.

nodes.name: Verify index equality
nodes.statement: From \eqref{uff} applied to $\phi^{-1}$ and $\psi^{-1}$ we have $C(\psi^{-1},\xi(U))=\xi(C(\phi^{-1},U))$, so, using also the fact that $\xi$ is an isomorphism, \begin{equation*}\begin{split} [\psi(C(\psi^{-1},\xi(U))):C(\psi^{-1},\xi(U))]=[\psi(\xi(C(\phi^{-1},U))):\xi(C(\phi^{-1},U))]=\\ =[\xi(\phi(C(\phi^{-1},U))):\xi(C(\phi^{-1},U))]=[\phi(C(\phi^{-1},U)):C(\phi^{-1},U)]; \end{split}\end{equation*} then \eqref{suff} is verified and this concludes the proof.
nodes.statement_short: Transport indices through $\xi$.

nodes.name: Monotonicity
nodes.statement: Let $G$ be a totally disconnected locally compact group, $\phi:G\to G$ a topological automorphism and $N$ a closed normal subgroup of $G$ such that $\phi(N)=N$, and let $\overline\phi:G/N\to G/N$ be the topological automorphism induced by $\phi$. Then: \begin{itemize} \item[(a)] $C(\phi\restriction_N,U\cap N)=C(\phi,U)\cap N$ for every $U\in\mathcal B(G)$, and $h_{top}(\phi)\geq h_{top}(\phi\restriction_N)$; \item[(b)] $C(\overline\phi,q(U))=q(C(\phi,U))$ for every $U\in\mathcal B(G)$ such that $N\subseteq U$, where $q:G\to G/N$ is the canonical projection; moreover, $h_{top}(\phi)\geq h_{top}(\overline\phi)$. \end{itemize}
assumptions: $G$ be a totally disconnected locally compact group, $\phi:G\to G$ a topological automorphism and $N$ a closed normal subgroup of $G$ such that $\phi(N)=N$
$\overline\phi:G/N\to G/N$ be the topological automorphism induced by $\phi$
conclusions: $C(\phi\restriction_N,U\cap N)=C(\phi,U)\cap N$ for every $U\in\mathcal B(G)$, and $h_{top}(\phi)\geq h_{top}(\phi\restriction_N)$
$C(\overline\phi,q(U))=q(C(\phi,U))$ for every $U\in\mathcal B(G)$ such that $N\subseteq U$, where $q:G\to G/N$ is the canonical projection; moreover, $h_{top}(\phi)\geq h_{top}(\overline\phi)$
nodes.statement_short: Topological entropy does not increase when passing to a $\phi$-invariant closed normal subgroup or to the quotient.
nodes.label: monotonicity

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 4.4
nodes.statement: (a) The first assertion is clear. Let $V\in \mathcal B(N)$. Then $V= U\cap N$ for some $U\in\mathcal B(G)$. We verify that $$H_{top}(\phi\restriction_N,V)\leq H_{top}(\phi,U)$$ and this implies the wanted inequality. By the first assertion in item (a), $C((\phi\restriction_N)^{-1},V)=C(\phi^{-1},U)\cap N$, so Fact \ref{gi}(c) gives \begin{equation*}\begin{split} [\phi\restriction_N(C((\phi\restriction_N)^{-1},V)):C((\phi\restriction_N)^{-1},V)]&=[\phi(C(\phi^{-1},U)\cap N):C(\phi^{-1},U)\cap N]\\&\leq[\phi(C(\phi^{-1},U)):C(\phi^{-1},U)]. \end{split}\end{equation*} By Theorem \ref{lf+}, taking the logarithms, this inequality gives $H_{top}(\phi\restriction_N,V)\leq H_{top}(\phi,U)$. \smallskip (b) The proof of the first assertion is straightforward. Let $q:G\to G/N$ be the canonical projection and $q(U)\in\mathcal B(G/N)$, where $U\in\mathcal B(G)$; we can assume without loss of generality that $N\subseteq U$. Since $N\subseteq C(\phi^{-1},U)$, by the first assertion in item (b) and Fact \ref{gi}(d) we have \begin{equation*}\begin{split} [\overline\phi(C(\overline\phi^{-1},q(U))):C(\overline\phi^{-1},q(U))]=[\overline\phi(q(C(\phi^{-1},U))):q(C(\phi^{-1},U))]=\\ =[q(\phi(C(\phi^{-1},U))):q(C(\phi^{-1},U))]]=[\phi(C(\phi^{-1},U)):C(\phi^{-1},U)]. \end{split}\end{equation*} Theorem \ref{lf+} applies to this equality and gives $H_{top}(\overline\phi,q(U))=H_{top}(\phi,U)$, hence we can conclude that $h_{top}(\overline\phi)\leq h_{top}(\phi)$.
nodes.statement_short: For subgroup and quotient, compare the limit-free indices using Fact 2.1(c) and 2.1(d), then apply Theorem 2.4.

nodes.name: (a) subgroup
nodes.statement: (a) The first assertion is clear. Let $V\in \mathcal B(N)$. Then $V= U\cap N$ for some $U\in\mathcal B(G)$. We verify that $$H_{top}(\phi\restriction_N,V)\leq H_{top}(\phi,U)$$ and this implies the wanted inequality. By the first assertion in item (a), $C((\phi\restriction_N)^{-1},V)=C(\phi^{-1},U)\cap N$, so Fact \ref{gi}(c) gives \begin{equation*}\begin{split} [\phi\restriction_N(C((\phi\restriction_N)^{-1},V)):C((\phi\restriction_N)^{-1},V)]&=[\phi(C(\phi^{-1},U)\cap N):C(\phi^{-1},U)\cap N]\\&\leq[\phi(C(\phi^{-1},U)):C(\phi^{-1},U)]. \end{split}\end{equation*} By Theorem \ref{lf+}, taking the logarithms, this inequality gives $H_{top}(\phi\restriction_N,V)\leq H_{top}(\phi,U)$.
nodes.statement_short: Fact 2.1(c) and Theorem 2.4 bound the entropy of the restriction.

nodes.name: (b) quotient
nodes.statement: (b) The proof of the first assertion is straightforward. Let $q:G\to G/N$ be the canonical projection and $q(U)\in\mathcal B(G/N)$, where $U\in\mathcal B(G)$; we can assume without loss of generality that $N\subseteq U$. Since $N\subseteq C(\phi^{-1},U)$, by the first assertion in item (b) and Fact \ref{gi}(d) we have \begin{equation*}\begin{split} [\overline\phi(C(\overline\phi^{-1},q(U))):C(\overline\phi^{-1},q(U))]=[\overline\phi(q(C(\phi^{-1},U))):q(C(\phi^{-1},U))]=\\ =[q(\phi(C(\phi^{-1},U))):q(C(\phi^{-1},U))]]=[\phi(C(\phi^{-1},U)):C(\phi^{-1},U)]. \end{split}\end{equation*} Theorem \ref{lf+} applies to this equality and gives $H_{top}(\overline\phi,q(U))=H_{top}(\phi,U)$, hence we can conclude that $h_{top}(\overline\phi)\leq h_{top}(\phi)$.
nodes.statement_short: Fact 2.1(d) and Theorem 2.4 give equal local entropies for the quotient.

nodes.name: Logarithmic law fails for negative powers
nodes.statement: Note that in the compact case $h_{top}(\phi)=h_{top}(\phi^{-1})$ and so the Logarithmic law extends to all integers. This is not possible in general in the locally compact case, as follows immediately from Proposition \ref{^-1}, where the modulus of $\phi$ is involved.

nodes.name: Logarithmic law
nodes.statement: Let $G$ be a totally disconnected locally compact group, $\phi:G\to G$ a topological automorphism and $k$ a positive integer. Then $h_{top}(\phi^k)=k\cdot h_{top}(\phi)$.
assumptions: $G$ be a totally disconnected locally compact group, $\phi:G\to G$ a topological automorphism and $k$ a positive integer

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 4.5 (Logarithmic law)
nodes.statement: Let $U\in\mathcal B(G)$ and denote $C=C(\phi^{-1},U)$. We start noting that $$C=C(\phi^{-k},V),\ \text{where}\ V=C_k(\phi^{-1},U).$$ Moreover, $\phi^{n+1}(C)\supseteq \phi^n(C)$ and $[\phi^{n+1}(C):\phi^n(C)]=[\phi(C):C]$ for every $n\geq0$, applying the automorphism $\phi^{-n}$. Then Fact \ref{gi}(a) gives \begin{align*} [\phi^k(C):C]&=[\phi^k(C):\phi^{k-1}(C)]\cdot[\phi^{k-1}(C):\phi^{k-2}(C)]\cdot\ldots\cdot[\phi(C):C]\\ &=[\phi(C):C]^k. \end{align*} Therefore, $$[\phi^k(C(\phi^{-k},V)):C(\phi^{-k},V)]=[\phi^k(C):C]=[\phi(C):C]^k;$$ so Theorem \ref{lf+} implies $$H_{top}(\phi^k,V)=k\cdot H_{top}(\phi,U).$$ This immediately gives $h_{top}(\phi^k)\geq k\cdot h_{top}(\phi)$. By Lemma \ref{antim}, since $V\subseteq U$, we have also $$H_{top}(\phi^k,U)\leq H_{top}(\phi^k,V)=k \cdot H_{top}(\phi,U),$$ so the missing converse inequality $h_{top}(\phi^k)\leq k\cdot h_{top}(\phi)$ holds as well, and this concludes the proof.
nodes.statement_short: Write $C(\phi^{-1},U)$ as the $\phi^{-k}$-cotrajectory of $V=C_k(\phi^{-1},U)$ and multiply indices. Lemma 4.1 gives the converse inequality.

nodes.name: Rewrite cotrajectory
nodes.statement: Let $U\in\mathcal B(G)$ and denote $C=C(\phi^{-1},U)$. We start noting that $$C=C(\phi^{-k},V),\ \text{where}\ V=C_k(\phi^{-1},U).$$
nodes.statement_short: Set $C=C(\phi^{-1},U)=C(\phi^{-k},V)$.

nodes.name: Multiply indices
nodes.statement: Moreover, $\phi^{n+1}(C)\supseteq \phi^n(C)$ and $[\phi^{n+1}(C):\phi^n(C)]=[\phi(C):C]$ for every $n\geq0$, applying the automorphism $\phi^{-n}$. Then Fact \ref{gi}(a) gives \begin{align*} [\phi^k(C):C]&=[\phi^k(C):\phi^{k-1}(C)]\cdot[\phi^{k-1}(C):\phi^{k-2}(C)]\cdot\ldots\cdot[\phi(C):C]\\ &=[\phi(C):C]^k. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Fact 2.1(a) gives $[\phi^k(C):C]=[\phi(C):C]^k$.

nodes.name: Lower bound
nodes.statement: Therefore, $$[\phi^k(C(\phi^{-k},V)):C(\phi^{-k},V)]=[\phi^k(C):C]=[\phi(C):C]^k;$$ so Theorem \ref{lf+} implies $$H_{top}(\phi^k,V)=k\cdot H_{top}(\phi,U).$$ This immediately gives $h_{top}(\phi^k)\geq k\cdot h_{top}(\phi)$.
nodes.statement_short: Theorem 2.4 gives $H_{top}(\phi^k,V)=kH_{top}(\phi,U)$, hence $\ge$.

nodes.name: Upper bound
nodes.statement: By Lemma \ref{antim}, since $V\subseteq U$, we have also $$H_{top}(\phi^k,U)\leq H_{top}(\phi^k,V)=k \cdot H_{top}(\phi,U),$$ so the missing converse inequality $h_{top}(\phi^k)\leq k\cdot h_{top}(\phi)$ holds as well, and this concludes the proof.
nodes.statement_short: Antimonotonicity gives the converse inequality.

nodes.name: Continuity with respect to inverse limits
nodes.statement: Let $G$ be a totally disconnected locally compact group and $\phi:G\to G$ a topological automorphism. If $\{N_i:i\in I\}$ is a directed system of closed normal subgroups of $G$ with $\phi(N_i)=N_i$ and $\bigcap_{i\in I} N_i=\{1\}$, then $G\cong \varprojlim G/N_i$ and $h_{top}(\phi)=\sup_{i\in I} h_{top}(\overline \phi_i)$, where $\overline \phi_i:G/N_i\to G/N_i$ is the continuous endomorphism induced by $\phi$.
assumptions: $G$ be a totally disconnected locally compact group and $\phi:G\to G$ a topological automorphism
$\{N_i:i\in I\}$ is a directed system of closed normal subgroups of $G$ with $\phi(N_i)=N_i$ and $\bigcap_{i\in I} N_i=\{1\}$

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 4.6
nodes.statement: By Proposition \ref{monotonicity}(b) the inequality $h_{top}(\phi)\geq\sup_{i\in I}h_{top}(\overline\phi_i)$ holds. So let $U\in\mathcal B(G)$. There exists $i\in I$ such that $N_i\subseteq U$. Let $q_i:G\to G/N_i$ be the canonical projection. Since $N_i\subseteq C(\phi^{-1},U)$, by Proposition \ref{monotonicity}(b) and Fact \ref{gi}(d) we have \begin{equation*}\begin{split} [\overline\phi_i(C(\overline\phi_i^{-1},q_i(U))):C(\overline\phi_i^{-1},q_i(U))]=[\overline\phi_i(q_i(C(\phi^{-1},U))):q_i(C(\phi^{-1},U))]\\ =[q_i(\phi(C(\phi^{-1},U))):q_i(C(\phi^{-1},U))]=[\phi(C(\phi^{-1},U)):C(\phi^{-1},U)]. \end{split}\end{equation*} Theorem \ref{lf+} applies to this equality and gives $H_{top}(\overline\phi_i,q_i(U))=H_{top}(\phi,U)$. Therefore $H_{top}(\phi,U)\leq h_{top}(\overline\phi_i)$, hence we can conclude that $h_{top}(\phi)\leq\sup_{i\in I}h_{top}(\overline\phi_i)$.
nodes.statement_short: Monotonicity gives $\ge$; for $\le$ choose $N_i\subseteq U$ and use the limit-free formula on the quotient.

nodes.name: Easy inequality
nodes.statement: By Proposition \ref{monotonicity}(b) the inequality $h_{top}(\phi)\geq\sup_{i\in I}h_{top}(\overline\phi_i)$ holds.
nodes.statement_short: Monotonicity gives $\ge$.

nodes.name: Choose N_i inside U
nodes.statement: So let $U\in\mathcal B(G)$. There exists $i\in I$ such that $N_i\subseteq U$. Let $q_i:G\to G/N_i$ be the canonical projection.
nodes.statement_short: Pick $N_i\subseteq U$ and its projection $q_i$.

nodes.name: Index equality
nodes.statement: Since $N_i\subseteq C(\phi^{-1},U)$, by Proposition \ref{monotonicity}(b) and Fact \ref{gi}(d) we have \begin{equation*}\begin{split} [\overline\phi_i(C(\overline\phi_i^{-1},q_i(U))):C(\overline\phi_i^{-1},q_i(U))]=[\overline\phi_i(q_i(C(\phi^{-1},U))):q_i(C(\phi^{-1},U))]\\ =[q_i(\phi(C(\phi^{-1},U))):q_i(C(\phi^{-1},U))]=[\phi(C(\phi^{-1},U)):C(\phi^{-1},U)]. \end{split}\end{equation*}
nodes.statement_short: Fact 2.1(d) equates the quotient and original indices.

nodes.name: Conclude
nodes.statement: Theorem \ref{lf+} applies to this equality and gives $H_{top}(\overline\phi_i,q_i(U))=H_{top}(\phi,U)$. Therefore $H_{top}(\phi,U)\leq h_{top}(\overline\phi_i)$, hence we can conclude that $h_{top}(\phi)\leq\sup_{i\in I}h_{top}(\overline\phi_i)$.
nodes.statement_short: Theorem 2.4 gives the reverse inequality.

nodes.name: Weak Addition Theorem
nodes.statement: Let $G$ and $H$ be totally disconnected locally compact groups, $\phi:G\to G$ and $\psi:H\to H$ topological automorphisms. Then $h_{top}(\phi\times \psi)=h_{top}(\phi)+h_{top}(\psi)$.
assumptions: $G$ and $H$ be totally disconnected locally compact groups, $\phi:G\to G$ and $\psi:H\to H$ topological automorphisms

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 4.7
nodes.statement: Let $\eta=\phi\times\psi$. Since the family $\mathcal B=\mathcal B(G)\times\mathcal B(H)$ is a local base at $1$ of $G\times H$, in view of Corollary \ref{basesuff} it suffices to take $U\in\mathcal B(G)$ and $V\in\mathcal B(H)$, and to verify that $$H_{top}(\eta,U\times V)=H_{top}(\phi,U)+H_{top}(\psi,V);$$ this holds since $C(\eta^{-1},U\times V)=C(\phi^{-1},U)\times C(\psi^{-1},V)$, so $$[\eta(C(\eta^{-1},U\times V)):C(\eta^{-1},U\times V)]=[\phi(C(\phi^{-1},U)):C(\phi^{-1},U)]\cdot[\psi(C(\psi^{-1},V)):C(\psi^{-1},V)],$$ and Theorem \ref{lf+} concludes the proof.
nodes.statement_short: By Corollary 4.2 use product neighbourhoods; the cotrajectory of a product is the product, so indices multiply.
